author: Andrew Cruz
title: Long term project to bring faster MTA subway service in Brooklyn and Queens - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Cruz ,
2 hours ago
NEW YORK (PIX11) — Work is set to begin to bring faster train service on two busy subway lines in Brooklyn and Queens.
The largest signal and track replacement in the history of the MTA will begin on the A and C lines, Governor Kathy Hochul announced on Thursday.
More Transit News The $1.9 billion project, funded through congestion pricing, will include replacing signals that were installed in the 1930s with the modern Communications-Based Train Control. The new signal system allows trains to run faster and closer together. In the end, subway service will run with more frequency and be more reliable.
“Upgrading nearly 100-year-old signals does more than just modernize infrastructure that is long overdue – it is a critical part of our plan to run better and more frequent subway service, shortening waits and slashing delays,” said Hochul. “When this project is done, hundreds of thousands of A and C train riders will benefit from the world-class service on new, modern trains that New Yorkers deserve.”
The brand-new signals will be installed between High Street station in Brooklyn and Ozone Park-Lefferts Boulevard in Queens.
In addition to track and signal work, infrastructure work to support future cell phone service will also be done.
The ambitious project is not expected to be completed until 2032.
